The business soon repaid the initial outlay on advertising.

cards.def: to describe something as larger or more important than it really is
ex: He tends to overstate the case for reform.
The report may overstate the risk of infection.

cards.def: to express something written or spoken using different words
ex: Students learn to paraphrase a text in their own words.
To paraphrase the author, change is always difficult.

cards.def: to decide or arrange something in advance.
ex: The judges should not predetermine the outcome of the contest.
The driver used a map to predetermine the route.

cards.def: a device that shines images or films onto a screen or wall.
ex: They set up the projector to show the slides.
The teacher connected a video projector to the laptop.

cards.def: to change the structure or appearance of a building or room.
ex: They hired a builder to remodel the kitchen.
The couple spent a year saving to remodel the house.

cards.def: To say something again in a different or clearer way.
ex: Please restate your position so the whole committee can understand it.
The teacher asked us to restate the problem in simpler words.

cards.def: The bottom part of a foot or shoe.
ex: The hot sand burned the soles of their bare feet.
These boots have a thick rubber sole for better grip.

cards.def: The band of colors seen when light passes through a prism.
ex: A rainbow shows the full visible spectrum of sunlight.
Each color in the spectrum has a different wavelength.

cards.def: a person whose job is to buy and sell shares for other people
ex: She followed her stockbroker's advice and sold the shares early.
He worked as a stockbroker in the city for ten years.

cards.def: happening soon; about to take place
ex: Both parties are preparing for the upcoming election.
The poster listed every upcoming event at the hall.

cards.def: to leave a place or room so that someone else can use it
ex: Guests must vacate their rooms by 11 a.m. on the day of departure.
Tenants were given a month to vacate the premises.

cards.def: a set of exercises for the body and mind using postures and breathing
ex: I do yoga twice a week to relax and stay flexible.
She signed up for a morning yoga class at the gym.

cards.def: the basic unit of money used in China
ex: The bus ticket cost only about ten yuan.
The yuan rose slightly against the dollar this week.

cards.def: Kind and careful about the feelings and needs of others.
ex: It was very considerate of him to wait for us.
She is always polite and considerate towards her employees.

cards.def: Based on the number ten; counted or divided in tens.
ex: Move the decimal point two places to the right.
The figure is accurate to two decimal places.

cards.def: a current of cool air moving through an enclosed space.
ex: I felt a cold draft coming from the open window.
They put a towel down to block the draft under the door.

cards.def: Relating to the legal duty to act in someone else's best interests, especially with money.
ex: Directors have a fiduciary duty to protect their shareholders.
A financial adviser enters a fiduciary relationship with each client.

cards.def: a failure of a machine or part to work correctly
ex: A computer malfunction delayed all the flights.
Engineers found a malfunction in the cooling system.

cards.def: a piece of clothing combining trousers and a top, worn to protect clothes while working
ex: The painter put on a pair of white overalls.
The mechanic wiped his hands on his blue overalls.

cards.def: the basic unit of money in Mexico and several other Latin American countries
ex: The Mexican peso weakened sharply against the US dollar this week.
The peso fell to a record low on the currency markets.

cards.def: the activity of searching an area for gold, oil, or other minerals
ex: Thousands of people went prospecting for gold in the mountains.
They developed a new prospecting method to locate oil deposits.

cards.def: a printed document that describes a company, school, or plan to attract people
ex: Investors studied the company prospectus before buying any shares.
She requested the college prospectus to learn about available courses.

cards.def: a small bag used to carry money and personal items
ex: She bought a small leather purse for the trip.
She kept her keys and phone in her purse.

cards.def: in accordance with a law, rule, or agreement
ex: The company must report its earnings pursuant to the law.
Payment will be made pursuant to the agreement signed last month.

cards.def: a hot room where people sit to sweat and relax, popular in Finland.
ex: After the gym, they decided to have a sauna.
The hotel sauna was open until ten each evening.

cards.def: a long comfortable seat for two or more people.
ex: They sat on the sofa watching television.
A large leather sofa faced the fireplace.

cards.def: casual trousers for men or women.
ex: He wore a pair of gray slacks to the interview.
She changed into casual slacks after work.

cards.def: to soak something in liquid for a period of time
ex: Steep the tea leaves in hot water for five minutes.
Let the dried fruit steep overnight before baking.

cards.def: to think that someone or something is worth less than they really are
ex: Buyers often undervalue a property before bidding.
Managers should never undervalue someone's work.

cards.def: a game in which two teams hit a ball over a high net with their hands
ex: They played beach volleyball all afternoon in the warm sun.
The hotel built a volleyball court right next to the pool.

cards.def: the place where someone lives; a home
ex: Welcome to my humble abode; please come inside and sit down.
The man was homeless and had no fixed abode at all.

cards.def: buying something in one market and selling it in another to profit from price differences
ex: Sharp traders quickly spotted an arbitrage opportunity between the two markets.
The fund made millions by engaging in careful currency arbitrage.

cards.def: to think of many ideas quickly, especially as a group
ex: The team met to brainstorm ideas for the campaign.
Let's brainstorm a list of possible solutions together.

cards.def: to strike repeatedly and violently, especially of wind or waves
ex: Huge waves buffet the rocky coast each winter.
The small tent was badly buffeted by icy winds.

cards.def: an apartment in a building where each unit is owned separately
ex: They bought a luxury condominium overlooking the bay.
A new condominium complex is being built downtown.

cards.def: to decorate something or someone, often for a special occasion
ex: The hall was decked out in flowers and balloons.
The streets were decked with flags for the parade.

cards.def: of very high quality and luxury
ex: They upgraded to a deluxe room with an ocean view.
Fans rushed to buy the deluxe edition of the album.

cards.def: a moving staircase that carries people between floors of a building
ex: We took the escalator up to the third floor.
She stumbled on the crowded escalator during the evening rush.

cards.def: to make a process happen more quickly
ex: We hired more staff to expedite the approval process.
They paid extra to expedite delivery of the package.

cards.def: a process that separates materials by making some particles float to the surface
ex: Froth flotation is widely used to separate valuable minerals from waste rock.
Engineers refined the flotation process to recover more copper from the ore.

cards.def: to fail or break down, especially because of a particular problem
ex: The peace talks foundered over disagreements about borders.
The project foundered on a lack of funding and support.

cards.def: the part of a telephone that you hold to your ear and speak into
ex: She lifted the handset and dialed the number slowly.
He carried the cordless handset into the kitchen while talking.

cards.def: as a result of this formal statement or act
ex: I hereby declare the new library officially open.
Both parties hereby agree to the terms of the contract.

cards.def: containing fewer calories or less fat than the standard product.
ex: She switched to lite beer to reduce her calorie intake.
The store sells several brands of lite yogurt.

cards.def: to move or guide something skillfully, especially into a position.
ex: The driver slowly maneuvered the truck into position.
He carefully maneuvered the boat through the narrow channel.

cards.def: able to be discussed and changed before an agreement is reached.
ex: The seller said the price was negotiable if we paid in cash.
They offered a negotiable contract with flexible working hours.

cards.def: to do better than someone or something else at a task or activity.
ex: The new phone easily outperforms its competitors in speed.
The fund managed to outperform the market last year.

cards.def: to move a camera steadily in one direction to follow something or show a wide view.
ex: The director asked them to pan the camera across the crowd.
The shot slowly pans across the empty battlefield.

cards.def: Arriving or doing something at the exact time arranged.
ex: She is always punctual and never misses a morning meeting.
The manager praised his punctual arrival every single day.

cards.def: to replace an existing loan with a new one, usually at better terms.
ex: The company took out a new loan to refinance its existing debt.
Homeowners rushed to refinance at a lower rate last year.

cards.def: a bag with shoulder straps carried on the back.
ex: He carried a heavy backpack on the long hike.
He set off with a backpack on his back.

cards.def: a car with a closed body and a separate trunk, seating four or more.
ex: They arrived in a sleek luxury sedan.
She drives a small sedan to work each day.

cards.def: one of the two main periods that a school or college year is divided into.
ex: She is taking five classes in the fall semester.
Students must complete three essays during the semester.

cards.def: unwanted email sent to many people, usually advertising something.
ex: Filters block most email spam before it arrives.
The spam filter caught the suspicious message.

cards.def: The extra benefit produced when people or things work together, greater than their separate effects.
ex: Combining their skills created synergy across the whole department.
There is clear synergy between the design and marketing teams.

cards.def: to sell something, especially in small amounts or to the public
ex: Street traders vend goods from carts along the busy avenue.
Only approved sellers are licensed to vend inside the stadium.

cards.def: a long-term loan to a company that pays fixed interest but is not secured by assets
ex: The firm decided to issue a debenture to raise new capital.
Investors bought the convertible debenture hoping to gain company shares.

cards.def: a person or company that rents property or equipment from its owner under a lease
ex: Under the contract, the lessee is responsible for all repairs.
The lease clearly lists the lessee's obligations and payment dates.

cards.def: a person or company that leases property or equipment to someone else
ex: The lessor and the lessee signed the agreement.
The tenant must pay the lessor each month.
